name: Acmer K1 3.5W
tagline: Entry K1: an enclosed 2.4 kg mini diode for engraving small objects under $200
tldr: The K1 3.5W is the cheapest version of Acmer's enclosed mini engraver still in stock in October 2026: a 150 × 150 mm area in a 2.4 kg box with lid and tilt sensors and an exhaust fan, for $199.99. It is an engraver first: wood, leather, paper and dark acrylic. Acmer's chart gives up to 8 mm of plywood, without stating the number of passes; in practice, cutting is slow and limited to thin material.
mainObjective: Safe, low-cost engraving of small objects at home

engraveExample.description: Filled photo or logo on birch plywood

cutExample.description: Simple square cut-out from 3 mm basswood

cut: Thin plywood and paulownia (Acmer chart: up to 8 and 10 mm, passes not stated)

pros: Enclosed box with lid and tilt sensors for $199.99
Plenty for engraving paper, card, leather and wooden gifts
Same box and software as the more powerful versions, with LightBurn support
cons: Slow: about 25–35 min for a 10 × 10 cm photo on plywood in our benchmark profile
Cutting 3 mm wood takes several passes, about 15–25 min for a 10 × 10 cm square
beginnerNotes: This profile is the 3.5W version of the Acmer K1. Compare it with the 7W: pick the 3.5W only if you will engrave and almost never cut; for $30 more, the 7W engraves faster and cuts thin wood. The box, area and software are identical.
proTips: Use high power and moderate speed for dark, even engraving on wood, and keep cutting for paper, card and felt. Vent the exhaust hose outside even for short jobs.

faq.question: Is the K1 3.5W enough for a beginner?
faq.answer: For engraving small objects, yes: wood, leather, paper and dark acrylic within 150 × 150 mm. If you hope to cut plywood shapes, take the 7W or 12W: the 3.5W cuts thin wood only with many slow passes.

faq.question: K1 3.5W or K1 7W?
faq.answer: Only $30 apart ($199.99 against $229.99 on Acmer's store, October 2026). The 7W engraves a 10 × 10 cm photo faster (about 18–26 min against 25–35 min in our benchmark profile) and cuts thin wood in reasonable time. For most buyers, the 7W is worth the difference.

faq.question: What about the K1 2.5W?
faq.answer: Acmer lists a 2.5W version at $179.99, but it was out of stock in October 2026. With even less power, it would only suit light engraving.

editorialDepth.advantages: The 3.5W is the lowest-cost way into an enclosed laser in Acmer's range: a closed box with safety sensors and an exhaust fan for under $200, which suits a first laser at home for paper, leather and wooden gifts.
editorialDepth.limitations: Engraving is slow and cutting is limited to thin material with many passes. For $30 more, the 7W does almost everything better; the 3.5W only makes sense if every dollar counts and you will not cut.

standoutFeatures.title: Enclosed for under $200
standoutFeatures.body: Lid sensor, tilt sensor and exhaust fan in a closed 2.4 kg box sold $199.99 on Acmer's store.

standoutFeatures.title: Open software choice
standoutFeatures.body: Works with ACMER Studio, LightBurn and LaserGRBL, so you can keep the same software if you move to a bigger laser.
